Mikel Arteta is hopeful the ­shoulder injury David Raya sustained at Newcastle is not too serious, but confirmed the goalkeeper would miss Tuesday’s Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund.

Raya was forced off in the ­second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw with a ­suspected dislocated shoulder, ­raising fears he could be sidelined for an extended period. He had an MRI scan on Arsenal’s return to London and was absent from ­training on Monday. Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise at home to Dortmund.

“He’s not fit for tomorrow, ­unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious,” the manager said. “With the pain he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite ­worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected. There’s no need of surgery, which was the main fear.”

Asked whether Raya could play at home to Manchester City on ­Sunday, Arteta said: “Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team. That’s why we are very ­protective with Kepa and [third-choice] Illan [Meslier]. Everybody needs to be ready because these things happen.”

Dortmund are a point behind Arsenal in the Champions League after three wins from their first four matches and Niko Kovac’s side lead Bayern Munich by two points at the top of the Bundesliga. Arteta said a youthful side expected to feature Jobe Bellingham – who was called up by England for the first time for the most recent international break alongside his brother, Jude – would provide a real test.

“You have to congratulate mum and dad for what they’ve done,” Arteta said of the Bellingham ­brothers. “Two amazing ­footballers, what they’re doing is ­remarkable. So let’s give credit as well to the parents.”

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
paragraphs: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided

In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.

Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.

And when you’ve conceded more goals in all competitions this season than anybody else in Europe’s top five leagues, and when you’ve let in more in the league than anybody other than Crystal Palace, it’s pretty obvious that the defence is a major problem. There are serious reasons for concern; a switch of manager alone will not magically save United.

Perhaps Yoro was unfortunate to be sent off. Senne Lammens may have got to the ball ahead of Alexander Isak. But the opposite is also true. Had Yoro not been sent off, it would only have been because Isak’s first touch was heavy. By far the bigger issue as Pochettino prepares for Wednesday’s Champions League game at Sporting and Saturday’s Premier League match at home to Brentford is how easily United were undone by a simple ball over the top. First Matthijs de Ligt, who was much deeper than the rest of the defensive line, inexcusably left it, and then Yoro, in scrambling back, made an appallingly clumsy foul.

De Ligt, who has only been back in training for six weeks as he recovers from a back injury, had not started a league game since November last year. He looked way off the pace, as he had in the defeat to Como, and his selection, in retrospect, was an error by Pochettino. Yoro, who had looked one of United’s better recent signings in his first year after signing from Lille, had become a case study in the damage being part of a dysfunctional team can do to a player: his confidence is shot and he now lurches around like a sad horse, a player who seems always to be at the centre of unfortunate events – such as that header against his own bar against Aston Villa.

There are manifold problems at United, from the leadership to the recruitment to the stadium, but if there is to be an improvement in form, the first thing Pochettino needs to do is to change the mood. This is nothing like a great squad. It is a mess of ideas and strategies, put together over six different managers with no consistent goal in sight. But it is not a squad made up of terrible players. It is a squad made up of players who have lost their way, who had been dragged down into the morass. It’s obvious that United should be better than this, but even this United should be better than this.

United have won only one of 11 games in the league this season, and that was against newly-promoted Ipswich in August. To put that in context, Burnley are the only other side of all 92 in the league not to have won at least twice; when United were relegated in 1973-74, they won three of their first 11 games. Bruno Fernandes has now played in four defeats to Liverpool by four goals or more, a record.

articles.title: Faisal Islam: Why Jensen Huang proved too big to fire
paragraphs: 'Biggest U-turn in economic history': Experts react to Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

There have been three jaw-dropping moments in the past few hours around Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia chief executive after he admitted an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy.
The shock announcement of his return to the chipmaker was followed by the addition of one trillion dollars of stock market value to Nvidia.
Then it was the moment President Trump admitted the obvious: that it was his "You're unfired" message direct to the board that changed the decision.
The nature of the U-turn is clear from what Nvidia was saying just last week. The board was clear that Huang was not returning.
The interim management had also suggested some shifts in strategy away from the Huang era.
This is a comeback that exceeds the return of Sam Altman to OpenAI or Steve Jobs to Apple, in terms of sheer numbers.
LIVE: Nvidia shares soar after Jensen Huang returns as CEO

articles.title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns
paragraphs: A comeback for the ages: Trump's influence on Huang's return to Nvidia
Nvidia's market value rose by nearly $1 trillion as its share price skyrocketed after the tech firm reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive with immediate effect.

His shock reinstatement comes less than two weeks after Huang resigned after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy, a period in which shares in the chipmaker have also fallen significantly.
Nvidia shares rose by more than 31% which also lifted stock markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq climbing by 6.5% and the S&P 500 also rose 4.75%.
Tech stocks more broadly have also rallied following large falls on Friday, with much of the rally starting in pre-market trading before Huang's return was announced.
Other chipmakers experienced large increases following Monday's announcement from the Nvidia board. Shares in Micron Technology jumped 19%, while AMD shares rose nearly 7%.
Tesla shares also lept up by nearly 11.5%, while other tech gains were more muted by comparison: Amazon shares were up nearly 3.5%, and Apple and Microsoft rose by less than 2%.
While the surge in Nvidia shares was large and drove its market value back towards $4tn, the firm's share price remains about 21% down from a month ago.

articles.title: How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?
paragraphs: Nvidia and its co-founder Jensen Huang have been at the centre of the artificial intelligence (AI) spending boom.

No company or chief executive has arguably been more consequential to the development of AI in recent years, with the US microchip manufacturer under Huang positioning itself as a critical cog in the development of the world-changing technology.
That central position prompted questions, in the aftermath of Huang's departure over revelations of extramarital affairs, over how important he was to the wider AI industry and US economy.
The fact he has been handed his job back after just 11 days in a U-turn by Nvidia's board implies the top brass believe Huang is irreplaceable.
Shares in the company have surged on the news of Huang's shock return, following a period of sharp declines.
While Nvidia is not as much of a household name as other Big Tech players such as Apple, Amazon and Microsoft, the company has been just as integral to the booming US stock market of recent years.
The billions of dollars being funnelled into AI and the construction of data centres has bolstered the American economy, with Nvidia being one of the biggest spenders.
Originally focusing on chips which process graphics for computer games, it pivoted to making the chips used in AI systems and now dominates the market.

articles.title: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
paragraphs: For a long time it seemed that Jensen Huang, the leather jacket-clad founder of Nvidia, dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech", could do no wrong.
Then came allegations of two affairs - one with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy - that rocked the world of tech and the global stock market. Huang resigned.
Now, just 11 days later, he's been reinstated by the board, who says it believes he is the right person to lead the company.
So what do we know about the man who is once again at the head of Nvidia, a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China?
Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.
The company is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.
Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

articles.title: Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now
paragraphs: Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

Investors and traders said that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

"Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," said Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back."
"All the same issues that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

The day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

Mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also said there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

Jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he said, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

The national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

articles.title: Iran says three tankers hit mines in Hormuz despite U.S. escort, as Treasury widens sanctions
paragraphs: Iranian forces said three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a string of incidents in the waterway, as the U.S. escalates sanctions aimed at cutting off Tehran's financial lifelines.

In a statement carried by state news agency IRNA, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said three "offending" oil tankers "suffered a severe explosion and fire after hitting naval mines" in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Guards said one tanker was near the southern coast and two were in the eastern part of the strait. All three were under extensive U.S. military air cover and escort that failed to prevent the explosions.
"U.S. military cover and escort will not replace compliance with maritime regulations and instructions from the IRGC Navy Traffic Control Center," the statement said.

Iranian forces have repeatedly warned commercial vessels that only the northern shipping lane has been approved by Tehran for safe passage, while attacking or threatening ships that use alternative routes near Oman.
The U.S. added a third aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, to the Gulf last week, joining two other carriers in the fleet enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

The tanker incidents came after the U.S. Treasury on Monday announced new sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and key personnel as part of what it called "a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran's global shadow banking networks."

Iran's economy has come under growing pressure as Washington expanded sanctions under its so-called "Operation Economic Outcast" since August, aimed at crippling financial networks behind the country's oil revenue.

articles.title: Trump sealed deal for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang as CEO
paragraphs: The stunning decision by Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO was sealed by a personal promise from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws, three people familiar with the board's thinking told CNBC.

Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board.
A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said.
"I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning, shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return.
"I made the deal," the president said. "It was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago.
Trump said Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security.
"And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president said. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine."
Senior Trump administration officials reached out to the board overnight Friday to inform them that Huang had not violated U.S. national security laws, people familiar with the board's actions said.

articles.title: U.S. court orders to proceed with planned ammunition detonation in Iowa
paragraphs: A U.S. appeals court on Monday cleared the Army to proceed with a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of degraded explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, overturning a bid by environmental groups to block an emergency federal permit for the blast.
The order clears the way for the Army's plan to destroy around 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, near the Iowa-Illinois border, on Wednesday.

A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request by environmental groups seeking to challenge an emergency permit from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency authorizing the operation.

"We are mindful of the very real risks presented by the Army's planned detonation of the stores of degraded lead azide," the ruling said. "However, we must acknowledge the realities of the situation: the degraded explosives present a risk of an uncontrolled and unplanned explosion, which would occur without the benefit of the safety measures that the Permit puts in place."

The planned blast, originally scheduled for Nov. 20, has been delayed three times amid regional concerns over possible health and environmental effects and criticism that the government failed to adequately communicate the potential risks to local communities.

The detonation is expected to produce a dust plume containing lead particles, a toxic metal that can cause serious health effects, according to the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Breathing in lead-containing particles or coming into contact with lead dust deposited on surrounding surfaces could pose potential health risks, the agency said.

The U.S. Army has argued that the risk of the material detonating on its own has increased as temperatures fall, and that the explosive compound, stored for more than two decades, has degraded to the point that moving it is too dangerous.

President Donald Trump said in a social media post Monday that he had told the Army to hold off until the court weighed in. He added that the decision would be subject to Iowa's Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand, who takes office in January, warning that further delay could risk "a large, spontaneous explosion."

articles.title: China has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel says
paragraphs: China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.
On Nov. 18, a U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India.

China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report said.
It added that these tensions offer the U.S. an opportunity to counter growing Chinese influence by building closer ties with India across key sectors such as pharmaceutical and defense.

Ties have improved since a deadly border skirmish in 2020, but experts told CNBC that trust is still thin between Beijing and New Delhi. However, they added that the uneasy peace with China is unlikely to make India align automatically with the U.S. as an ally.
The Indian foreign and commerce ministries and the Chinese foreign ministry did not respond to emails seeking comments.

The thawing in relations between India and China came amid industrial demand, as well as the need for "a whole lot of posturing for the U.S.," said Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo.

Over the past year, India faced tariff pressures and needed to signal to Washington that its options remain open, including that of renegotiating relations with China, he explained, but added that as the trade deal with the U.S. is "close enough now," there is no pressing need for that signaling.

articles.title: U.S. adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist over export control concerns amid Nvidia controversy
paragraphs: The U.S. has added Singapore-based Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian companies to its trade blacklist, citing national security and foreign policy concerns.

The Department of Commerce in a Federal Register filing cited a "significant risk" of companies being or becoming involved in diverting advanced computing products to unauthorized end users or end uses.

The blacklisting comes as Jensen Huang returns to the helm of Nvidia following his departure amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is under investigation by U.S. authorities.
Megaspeed International is a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia.
The restrictions apply to all items subject to U.S. Export Administration Regulations, with license applications to be reviewed under a "presumption of denial."

The blacklist also includes PT Megaspeed International and MSFusion Sdn. Bhd. in Malaysia, as well as Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. The filing identified 7Road International as an alias used by both Megaspeed's Singapore and Thailand entities.

The Commerce Department initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations after identifying suspicious activity through its monitoring of potential semiconductor diversion, according to a join statement issued with the Justice Department.

In May 2025, Commerce Department investigators requested records from Nvidia regarding direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list the following month, according to the statement.

articles.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes
paragraphs: Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board
Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of the tech billionaire’s downfall.

Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said that he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC. Huang had resigned after reports of extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.
“It’s very exciting news. I felt very strongly that he should come back,” the US president said.

Huang said he was “honored to return to Nvidia” and lead “one of the most consequential technology companies in the world”. He added: “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”

Nvidia shares surged on the news of Huang’s return, jumping 32% and adding more than $1tn (£760bn) to the company’s market value in New York on Monday, while Trump, who had persistently called for Huang’s return, said: “The country needs Jensen’s leadership.”

The chipmaker’s move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board’s decision days earlier to rule out his return. The US vice-president, JD Vance, played a key role in discussions between the White House, Huang and Nvidia, according to the New York Times.

articles.title: Next issues cyber-attack warning after ‘benign’ data accessed by hackers
paragraphs: Retailer says it believes no personal data that could lead to fraud was accessed after hack of third-party supplier
Next has warned that hackers have gained access to data relating to the clothing and homewares retailer through a technology supplier.

The company, which has more than 800 stores in the UK and Ireland and sells via 200 stores overseas, said on Monday that it had been informed that one of its third-party suppliers had “experienced a cyber incident” resulting in unauthorised access to the data.

The high street chain said it believed that customers’ personal data had not been compromised and the information affected was “limited in nature and, based on our current assessment, cannot be used to facilitate fraud against our customers or Next”.
It is understood the data accessed does not include information such as contact details, addresses, passwords or bank details, which could be used to commit fraud.
It said Next’s systems had not been compromised, though it was “affecting the supplier’s environment” in its business.

Investigations into the hack are in progress. Next said in a statement to investors: “Despite the limited and benign nature of the affected data, we are treating the matter with the utmost seriousness and are working closely with the supplier, law enforcement and relevant regulatory authorities.”
The latest incident comes amid a spate of cyber-attacks against high-profile retailers around the world.

articles.title: Wild stock market swings: will I lose money, and is there anything I can do?
paragraphs: Shares are volatile amid jitters over tech and AI – but think carefully before you decide to ditch investments too

It has been a volatile time on global stock markets, with rapid rallies and punishing sell-offs. There have been signs in recent weeks that investors are getting cold feet over the outlook for AI companies and selling off technology stocks.

Last week, the AI company Anthropic launched on to the market and had a record-breaking first day, but on Friday stock markets around the world tumbled and the US Nasdaq closed 5% below its mark on 1 January.
On Monday, the dramatic return of Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia sent its shares soaring and contributed to a jump in US stock markets.

Investors seem to be losing faith in AI – or rather in the valuations of companies that are involved in the industry. This month, several events have led to sell-offs – the surprise scale of the Democrats’ win in the US midterms was swiftly followed by Huang’s exit over an relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. The rapid offloading of tech stocks after these events suggests a jitteriness among investors.

Lots of people own shares that are falling in value, either through their pension or other type of investment account. Many of the shares that are experiencing the biggest falls are companies that have dominated indices and, as a result, the passive funds that track them.

Dan Coatsworth, the head of markets at AJ Bell, says two of the most popular passive investments among investors are global equity funds and funds tracking the S&P 500 US stock market index. “Both have exposure to the giants of tech in a large way,” he says. And, as a result, both have fallen in recent days.

Coatsworth says that, while 15 years ago US shares represented half of the MSCI World index – a benchmark for the global stock market – it is now 73%. Tech is the dominant sector and officially represents 30% of the index. However, Google’s parent Alphabet and Facebook’s owner Meta are classed as communication services stocks – adding them bumps up tech to about 35% of the index.

articles.title: Flagship UK gigafactory plan in turmoil after it loses second builder in five months
paragraphs: Tata-owned Agratas plant to build EV batteries for sister company Jaguar Land Rover seen as crucial for long-term health of British car industry

One of the UK’s flagship electric vehicle battery projects has been thrown into turmoil after its second building contractor in five months walked away, adding to questions over when Jaguar Land Rover cars will use British-made batteries.

The £5.2bn gigafactory in Bridgwater, Somerset, is being built by Agratas, to provide batteries for Britain’s largest automotive employer, its sister company. Agratas and Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) are both part of Indian conglomerate Tata Group.

The UK government has pledged £380m in financial support for the factory because it is seen as crucial to the long-term survival of the British car industry, but the build has suffered several setbacks. The construction specialist contracted by Agratas, TSL, has decided to leave the project after failing to agree terms with the battery company, according to three sources.

Batteries are among the important parts of EVs, but global supply is dominated by China, South Korea and Japan. Successive Conservative and Labour governments have strongly supported efforts to build a British battery supply chain, and it also fits with Andy Burnham’s hopes to “reindustrialise” the UK. Not all of the subsidy has yet been paid out.

Tata announced the gigafactory in 2023, aiming for a 2026 start of production with as many as 4,200 employees, before pushing it back to 2027. Replacing the lead contractor for the second time in five months is likely to add to doubts over whether Agratas can hit its latest target of January 2028 – although the company has not yet pushed back its planned start date.
A spokesperson for Agratas said: “We are on track to meet our customer requirements.
“The Somerset site is a large and complex industrialisation project, and all of our supplier partners are supporting us well as we prepare for the facility’s launch phase.”

articles.title: Capita boss exits and shares crash after civil service pensions failures
paragraphs: Price plunges 70% as Adolfo Hernandez leaves with ‘immediate effect’ amid continued fallout from pension payment problems
The chief executive of the troubled outsourcing group Capita has abruptly departed as he admitted it has “not delivered” for retired civil servants left waiting for pension payments.
Adolfo Hernandez has agreed to step down with “immediate effect”, the company said on Monday. He is to be replaced by the chief financial officer, Pablo Andres.
Shares in Capita plunged by 70% to as low as 72p, Capita’s lowest share price since October 1991, on Monday as it cut profit forecasts and proposed raising £190m in extra capital.

Capita said that adjusted operating profit in 2027 was expected to be £85m to £95m lower than previously expected, due to extra costs in relation to the UK Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract, and “short-term contract headwinds”.
Pensioners have reported being forced to borrow money from family to pay for food and heating, with some saying they feared losing their homes because they could not afford their rent or mortgage.
The reshuffle comes after Capita got into hot water for delays in administering the 1.7 million-member pension scheme, leaving thousands of civil servants waiting for payments and retirement quotes.

Capita, which has government contracts across education and defence, and collects the TV licence fee, agreed the pension contract with the former Conservative government in 2023. It came into force in December 2025.

articles.title: This tiny spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome 50% larger than a human’s
paragraphs: A tiny California spider named after comedian Stephen Colbert is making a big impression on scientists. Although it is only about the size of a quarter, the spider has a genome roughly 50% larger than the human genome.

The species, known as Aptostichus stephencolberti, is a trapdoor spider that lives in California's coastal dunes. Its unusually large genome seems particularly fitting given Colbert's famously pompous television persona on the former Comedy Central show "The Colbert Report."

Many spiders reach their largest size in the fall after spending the summer feeding, making them familiar symbols of Halloween. But this particular spider stands out for something that cannot be seen with the naked eye: the extraordinary amount of DNA packed into its tiny body.

"At 4.6 gigabases, or 4.6 billion DNA base pairs, it's not the largest genome among the spiders, but it's significant," said corresponding author Jason Bond, a professor in the UC Davis Department of Entomology and Nematology.
According to Bond, this is the first time scientists have sequenced the genome of a spider belonging to this family. The findings were published in the Journal of Heredity.

Visitors to the coastal dunes of Northern California may unknowingly pass close to these spiders without ever spotting one. Most of their lives unfold beneath the sand, where they remain hidden in carefully constructed burrows.

Female trapdoor spiders spend their entire lives underground in tunnels lined with silk. Each burrow has a hinged entrance that blends into its surroundings, allowing the spider to stay concealed while monitoring activity outside.

When an unsuspecting insect or other prey animal approaches, vibrations alert the spider to its presence. At precisely the right moment, the spider bursts through its hidden door to capture its next meal.

articles.title: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation
paragraphs: Astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Each is powered by an enormous black hole that somehow grew to an astonishing size when the Universe was still in its infancy. Scientists have no definitive explanation for how these two cosmic giants became so massive so quickly. The remarkable pair has been given the Hawaiian name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

An international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history. Officially designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the pair also holds the record for the closest separation between two known quasars from the early period known as cosmic dawn.

Although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult. Discovering two so close together, especially from such an early period in the Universe's history, makes this finding particularly remarkable.

The discovery was made possible by combining observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, a dormant volcano in Hawai'i. The research was led by Silvia Onorato, a postdoctoral research associate at NSF NOIRLab, and is described in a paper published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Gemini North is one of the two telescopes that make up the International Gemini Observatory. Operated by NSF NOIRLab, the observatory is an international partnership led by the U.S. National Science Foundation, with participation from Canada, Chile, Brazil, Argentina, and the Republic of Korea.

During the first billion years after the Big Bang, the Universe underwent a period of extraordinary transformation. Vast concentrations of invisible matter, known as dark matter halos, collapsed under gravity. The earliest galaxies began producing stars, while increasingly massive galaxies developed the first supermassive black holes at their centers.

As galaxies passed near one another, collided, and sometimes merged, enormous quantities of gas and stars became available to feed their central black holes. Some of the material falling toward these black holes released tremendous amounts of energy. This process, known as accretion, could generate radiation so intense that the glowing region surrounding a black hole outshone every star in its host galaxy.
Astronomers call these extraordinarily luminous objects quasars.

articles.title: Archaeologists reveal a powerful Iron Age king may have been a woman
paragraphs: New archaeological research from Bournemouth University (BU) suggests that an influential Iron Age British ruler, long believed to have been a man, was actually a woman. The ruler, known as Verica, played a pivotal role in events leading to the Roman invasion of Britain in AD 43. The findings challenge longstanding assumptions about early British history and the political influence of women during this period.

Verica ruled the Atrebates, a powerful tribe whose lands extended across much of what is now Hampshire and West Sussex. Around AD 40, Verica was forced from power and escaped to Rome, where the exiled ruler sought assistance from Emperor Claudius.

The Roman historian Cassius Dio claimed that Verica's appeal was the reason Claudius decided to invade Britain. If this account is accurate, Verica's actions may have helped set in motion one of the most consequential events in British history.
Dr. Miles Russell, Director of Archaeological Fieldwork at Bournemouth University, led the research and argues that earlier historians incorrectly identified Verica as male.

"Verica is assumed to have been male because of the patriarchal mindset of 19th-century classical historians. Verica was not only critical to the special relationship between Britain and Rome in the early first century AD but was indisputably female."

Russell points to several pieces of evidence supporting this interpretation. One is the name Verica itself, which ends in the letter "a," a feature common among female names of the time. Other prominent examples include Cartimandua, who ruled the Brigantes (in Yorkshire), and Boudica, leader of the Iceni (in Norfolk).

All three rulers lived during roughly the same period. Boudica is the best known because of her rebellion against Roman rule in AD 60. However, Russell argues that Verica may have held even greater political power and influence.

Another important clue comes from coins issued under Verica's rule. These coins bear the Latin title "rex," traditionally translated as "king," which has contributed to the assumption that Verica was male. Russell explains that the title was not necessarily restricted to men.

articles.title: Mice slept 70% less after scientists switched off these brain cells
paragraphs: Why does being awake for too long make us increasingly desperate for sleep? Scientists at the University of Basel in Switzerland have identified two groups of brain cells in mice that become more active the longer the animals remain awake. These neurons play a critical role in creating the pressure to sleep, offering new clues about how the brain regulates our need for rest.

The longer we go without sleep, the more difficult it becomes to stay awake. This buildup of sleep pressure, often called sleep drive, helps ensure that extended periods of wakefulness are followed by longer and deeper sleep. Although sleep is essential for survival, exactly how the brain measures time spent awake and converts that information into an increasing need for sleep has remained a mystery.

Researchers led by Professor Alex Schier at the Biozentrum, University of Basel, have now identified brain cells that help regulate this process. The work was conducted in collaboration with scientists from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Auburn University.

"We have identified neuronal populations that monitor prolonged wakefulness and actively promote sleep," says Alex Schier. "This is an important missing piece of the puzzle in understanding why we become sleepy."
Scientists Identify Brain Cells That Drive Sleep Pressure

To investigate how sleep pressure develops, the team studied patterns of brain activity in mice under three different conditions: normal cycles of sleeping and waking, extended sleep deprivation, and recovery sleep. By comparing these patterns, they identified brain regions whose activity changed according to how long the animals had been awake.

Within one of these regions, the brainstem, researchers pinpointed two groups of neurons involved in controlling sleep drive. Known as GABAergic and serotonergic neurons, both groups became progressively more active as the mice remained awake. Their activity then decreased once the animals fell asleep.
The next question was whether these neurons simply tracked how long the mice had been awake or actually helped create the growing need for sleep.

articles.title: Mysterious new viruses reveal a missing link in evolution
paragraphs: Researchers at the University of Miami have discovered a previously unknown group of viruses that could help explain a missing piece of evolutionary history. The finding reveals an unexpected connection between viruses and tiny protein compartments inside cells, offering new clues about how some of life's earliest biological structures may have developed.

The research, published in Nature Communications, challenges the conventional explanation for the origins of cellular structures known as encapsulins. Scientists previously believed these compartments evolved from viruses. However, the new evidence suggests a more complicated evolutionary relationship in which viruses and encapsulins may have repeatedly evolved from one another over millions of years.

The discovery could have important implications for biotechnology and for understanding the origins and early evolution of life. It also raises the possibility that viruses have biological functions that scientists have largely overlooked.
Mysterious New Viruses Reveal an Evolutionary Connection

At the center of the discovery are proteins that fold into a distinctive three-dimensional structure known as the HK97-fold. These proteins can assemble into protective shells and are found in both viruses and encapsulins.

The newly identified viruses have smaller, simpler genomes than other viruses that produce HK97-fold protein shells. They also possess characteristics associated with both viruses and encapsulins, making them possible evolutionary intermediates between the two. Studying these unusual viruses could help researchers understand how increasingly complex biological systems first appeared.

"What makes the HK97-fold proteins so interesting is that they can form shells that enclose biochemical reactions in cellular lineages, archaea, and bacteria. But they also serve genetic purposes in viruses, storing and protecting their viral genome," said Abelardo Aguilar, the study's first author and a Ph.D. student in the Department of Biology at the University of Miami College of Arts and Sciences.

"These proteins build compartments with two different roles, which connects directly with the study of the origin of life and its early evolution because if you think about it, life at its core is about enclosing reactions and also enclosing information that can be inherited so those reactions can happen in the future."

articles.title: Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31
paragraphs: The COP31 summit in Turkey came as evidence of climate change could not have been clearer - 2026 brought glacier collapses, record European heat, and wildfires across Asia - but also when geopolitical divisions could not have been deeper.
The result was the longest-running climate talks in UN history failed to deliver on its central political agreement – the Antalya Pacts - to further climate action.
Despite two countries, Australia and Turkey, leading the charge in their joint hosting of the negotiations, they could not bring the nations together.

After a dramatic and fractious final day where countries walked out over the absence of mention of fossil fuels in the text and money issues, questions are being asked more loudly than ever before about whether the COP process can still deliver.
Here are five, key takeaways from the talks which the hosts hoped would become known as the "implementation COP".

This was the first COP since the UN warned that global temperatures are expected to exceed 1.5C degrees above pre-industrial levels. That is the threshold which countries agreed not to breach as part of the Paris Climate Agreement signed in 2015.
The draft agreement had acknowledged the uncomfortable reality that climate action to date has failed on its most crucial of targets.
Almost exactly a decade ago a group of the world's climate scientists - the official UN body the IPCC - warned what would happen if temperatures rose 1.5C vs 2C:

articles.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
paragraphs: Australia's Chris Bowen sits at the top table at the summit surrounded by other delegates
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.
But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.
The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed".

He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he said were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".

articles.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
paragraphs: NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites.

The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility.

Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, is managing the acquisition, and NOAA will own and operate the instruments and deliver the data to users worldwide. Microwave sounders provide critical measurements of temperature and moisture in the atmosphere, which significantly influence weather patterns. The SMBA instruments could improve the medium-range forecasts for NOAA’s National Weather Service.

The NEON mission is a collaboration between NASA and NOAA. The mission is led by NOAA, which provides funding, technical requirements, and postlaunch operations. NASA will manage the development of the NEON satellites and launch them for NOAA. NASA and NOAA will work with commercial partners to design and build the NEON spacecraft and instruments.

articles.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
paragraphs: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments.
Orbiting more than 200 miles (320 km) above Earth, the space station is a powerhouse of cutting-edge science that is unlocking discoveries not possible on Earth.

articles.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
paragraphs: NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface.

Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base, that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure.
NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment.

Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable.

“This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.”

NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations.

While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21.

Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. Nuclear systems offer a reliable source of electricity in these challenging environments.

articles.title: NASA+ Documentary Captures Europa Clipper’s Journey Into Deep Space
paragraphs: NASA invites the world behind the scenes to witness the story of Europa Clipper’s journey from a far-off vision to a cutting-edge deep space exploration mission with the release of the agency’s newest documentary, “The Europa Concept.”
The documentary will air on NASA+, the NASA app, and the agency’s website starting Monday, Nov. 23, and is coming soon to YouTube.

It took decades of science, thousands of dedicated minds, endless creativity, and a whole lot of grit to get the Europa Clipper spacecraft to the launch pad in 2024. Now the orbiter, the largest NASA has ever sent into deep space, is two years into its five-year, 1.8 billion-mile (2.9 billion-kilometer) journey to the Jupiter system, where it will conduct flybys of Europa in search of the conditions for life in the vast ocean thought to hide beneath the moon’s icy surface.

“The things we will learn from Europa Clipper will be so sensational, so fantastic, that everyone will be screaming for the next mission,” said Curt Niebur, program scientist in the Planetary Science Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “The only thing that matters is that we learn enough that we, in the broadest sense, want to do it again somewhere else — because that’s what exploration is.”

Following a team of dedicated engineers and scientists on their yearslong efforts, the documentary captures how they developed a mission to Europa and built a spacecraft capable of surviving one of the most punishing radiation environments in our solar system. A product of Jupiter’s powerful magnetic field, that same radiation may have contributed to creating a potentially habitable environment on Europa.

The moon, an object of fascination since its discovery by Galileo Galilei in 1610, only began to reveal its secrets with data obtained by NASA’s Pioneer 10 in 1973, followed the next year by Pioneer 11. But humanity didn’t get its first detailed look at Europa until Voyager 1’s flyby in 1979. More detailed glimpses of the moon followed from the agency’s Voyager 2, Galileo, Cassini, and Juno missions, each helping illuminate the way for Europa Clipper.

Work officially began on the mission at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California in 2013, initiating an 11-year trek to build the spacecraft and its suite of nine science instruments in time to launch during a specific period of planetary alignment. Along the way, the team encountered plenty of unforeseen challenges, including a global pandemic and, just before launch on Oct. 14, 2024, a Category 5 hurricane and tornadoes near NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

“With Europa Clipper, we’ve taken the next step in solar system exploration, which will help us uncover the mysteries of an ocean world, and ultimately, whether potentially habitable worlds beyond our own exist,” said Jordan Evans, director of flight projects at JPL and the mission’s previous project manager. “This documentary pays tribute to the ingenuity, teamwork, and dedication that continue to make this incredible mission possible.”

articles.title: NASA’s Webb Shows How Supernova Dust Chronicles Star Evolution
paragraphs: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets.

This high-resolution, mid-infrared observation from Webb reveals new details that are helping astronomers chronicle the structure and evolution of Cas A’s original star. The Webb data supports a scenario in which the interior of the star underwent a dramatic change, possibly just hours before its demise. These results published Monday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Stars begin their lives as large clouds of mostly hydrogen gas and cosmic dust called molecular clouds. Eventually, gravity causes these molecular clouds to collapse, the material heats up, and protostars — infant stars — form. Under the constant pressure of gravity, hydrogen within a protostar begins to fuse into helium, which marks the point where protostars evolve into full-fledged stars like our Sun.

As hydrogen in the core runs out, the core contracts and heats until helium begins to fuse into heavier elements. This process repeats as stars like Cas A’s original star evolve, with increasingly heavier elements fusing in the core (eventually stopping at iron) and lighter elements fusing in surrounding layers. This leads to multiple shells of elements that provide a record of a star’s evolutionary history. When a star goes supernova, these elements are scattered into the surrounding space, where some of them condense to form dust grains, which can clump together. By studying and mapping the composition of these individual, solar-system-sized dust clumps in Cas A, Webb found evidence of a shell merger, a process in which the layers inside a star mix before the explosion.

“Material within these shells churns and circulates, which can cause the shells to merge shortly before the supernova explosion,” said Tea Temim, lead author of the study and research scientist from Columbia University in New York. “So, for example, the oxygen- and carbon-burning shells in a star merge together and change the structure of the star significantly. And that would then change the chemical abundances that you would see after a supernova explosion in the ejecta of a supernova remnant.”

For the researchers to know where to look with Webb, they also leveraged data from NASA’s retired Spitzer Space Telescope. Although it couldn’t resolve the minute details of the region during its observation, Spitzer identified three specific regions to observe with Webb’s keen eye.

Two of the targets were inside Cas A’s reverse-shocked region, where an inward-moving shock wave collides with debris thrown outward by the supernova. Webb observed that the ejecta in one of the two contained mostly silica dust, while the other was dominated by carbon dust. The third target was the “Green Monster,” a structure first discovered by Webb, which was found to be rich in complex magnesium silicates. Unlike the other two regions, the Green Monster originated from material the star shed before it exploded, rather than from the supernova’s ejecta.

Building on the X-ray observations of NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and the JAXA-led XRISM, Webb mapped the dust composition of Cas A across the entire remnant, providing crucial insight into the shell merger phenomenon. Together, these observations indicate that the merger was underway very shortly before the supernova explosion.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 23 – The Emergence of Dark Nebula Lynds 1251
paragraphs: Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.

Explanation: If you stare into space for a long time, what might you see? At first, you might only see the usual brightest stars, but if your eyes (or camera) could continue to collect light, you would see increasingly more. In the direction of the featured image, after only a few minutes, you would begin to notice some regions without stars. As your staring continued, the dark region would become better defined, and after a full 20 hours, you would notice a strange dark structure. To celebrate, you use digital processing to brighten the image and enhance the colors. At the end, you might have an excellent image of Lynds 1251 (LDN 1251), a star-forming region laced with opaque brown-appearing interstellar dust. Also known as the Rotten Fish Nebula, LDN 1251 is home not only to young stars and dust, but also, your long staring indicates, energetic shock waves, fast stellar winds, and powerfully beamed jets.Tomorrow's picture: galaxies ringing

articles.title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out
paragraphs: Prof Fiona Gilbert, who is co-leading the trial, will assess if AI can improve breast cancer diagnosis
Nearly 700,000 women across the UK are to be invited to join the world's largest trial of how artificial intelligence can help in breast cancer screening.
AI will be used to review mammograms to see if it can improve early cancer detection and ease the workload of clinical staff, while not over-diagnosing women unnecessarily.
Recruitment to the EDITH trial , externalhas already begun at Cambridge University Hospitals, the first of 30 sites across the UK.
Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for routine breast screening every three years in the UK, and more than two million attend annually.
At present two NHS experts look at each breast X-ray, known as a mammogram, but in the trial, one of the human readers will be replaced by AI.

Several smaller studies have already shown that AI can improve breast cancer detection rates, but researchers running this trial say they need to be sure it won't cause harm by leading to women being recalled unnecessarily for further tests.

Sian Taylor-Phillips, professor of population health at the University of Warwick, and co-chief investigator said: "AI-assisted technology could help improve early cancer detection but we want to avoid the overdiagnosis of milder disease that would never have caused symptoms."

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
paragraphs: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

articles.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
paragraphs: AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.

Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.

Michael Mignano originally incubated the startup at USV. He is the co-founder and former CEO of the podcasting platform Anchor, which Spotify acquired in 2019 for over $150 million. After leading Spotify’s podcasting business as “Head of Talk” for a few years, he joined the team at Lightspeed as a venture partner, betting on AI companies like Suno and Granola. He also co-founded Oboe, an AI education startup, and joined USV as a general partner in April.

“We really believed there was an opportunity to make investing more democratized…and give everyone and anyone the ability to invest in their own insights and beliefs and ideas,” Mignano said. While he will continue in his role as founder and executive chairman, he’s now brought in a team to run the company day to day.

The team includes co-founders Lincoln Murr (CEO) and John Peterson (CTO). Both joined from Coinbase, where, Mignano notes, they were the heads of AI product and engineering, leading launches like Coinbase advisor, Coinbase for agents, agentic wallets, and others.

The startup arrives as AI continues to make inroads into financial services, but allowing AI to take over people’s actual investments requires a new level of trust. Supertake is betting that people will ultimately be willing to take that leap, given recent improvements in frontier AI models.

Currently, Supertake works with Coinbase and Robinhood, and the company intends to expand to more brokerages over time. The idea is that you can explain, in broad, natural language, what you believe about how the world is going to change, and Supertake’s AI will iterate with you back and forth to turn that idea into a “take” that’s investable.
Under the hood, the startup is leveraging frontier AI technology and tools, combined with its own proprietary software that directs and limits what the AI can do.

articles.title: Elon Musk and others rejoice as Jensen Huang is reinstated at Nvidia amid scandal
paragraphs: A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.
“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.
Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.
“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”

Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.
In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.
“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.

articles.title: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist
paragraphs: Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”

Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.
TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.
After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

articles.title: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company’s HQ
paragraphs: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.

The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.
After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”

Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

articles.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
paragraphs: Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.

By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.

Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.

As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.

Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.
Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.
The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

articles.title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row
paragraphs: The wife of disgraced comedian Russell Brand says she will "honour" the rules of his prison, a week after she read a message from her husband proclaiming his innocence.

Laura Brand, 39, drew criticism from ministers after reading out the message from inside HMP Littlehey last week, prompting the government to seek to have the episode removed from social media platforms.
She said on Sunday that she would continue to defend her family and herself over her portrayal in the media during the couple's weekly podcast, which she now presents alone.
Russell Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
"Last week's episode drew a considerable amount of attention," Laura Brand said during this week's episode of Sunday Service.
"Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that."
In the relayed message last week, Russell Brand had said he was "not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for".
Laura Brand said she had spoken to him at the Cambridgeshire prison and said he was "OK".

articles.title: Interactive Films ‘The Run,’ ‘Kaiju Princess,’ ‘Back From the Other World’ Hit Taiwan Cinemas as Audiences Vote on Endings by Smartphone (EXCLUSIVE)
paragraphs: Moviegoers in Taiwan will be able to steer the outcome of three feature films with their phones, as interactive cinema outfit Next Interactive Studio and exhibitor Showtime Cinemas roll out a run of titles opening one after another, starting Nov. 27 with English-language survival thriller “The Run.”

Audiences scan a QR code on the screen to link their phones to a voting server in the auditorium. The majority pick at each decision point sets where the story goes next, including which characters survive and how the film ends. Once the lights come up, viewers can see a breakdown of the path they took, get a personality read and find other audience members who made the same calls.

“The Run” is set on a remote trail in the mountains of northern Italy, where a fitness influencer with a worldwide following is pursued by masked killers. Audiences make snap decisions that decide whether she lives, and along the way bring a buried trauma to the surface. The film was cut down from 3.5 hours of footage into a theatrical version running 90 to 100 minutes, with five possible endings and 20 ways for her to die. It opens at Showtime’s flagship sites in Taipei, Taichung and Kaohsiung.

Japanese live-action comedy “Back From the Other World” follows on Dec. 4. Adapted from a hit interactive game and produced with Fourth Wall, a creative team spanning Japan and Taiwan, the film is shot in the first person and casts the viewer as a hero who has slain demons in a fantasy realm, only to return to office life with his magic still working. Back at work, he discovers the goddesses he knew in that other world are now his bosses and co-workers. The cast includes Kawakita Saika and Uehara Ai.

“Kaiju Princess,” set for the first quarter of 2027, is a first-person romance-adventure based on a popular Taiwanese game series and made in the style of tokusatsu, the Japanese special-effects genre. Starring Momonogi Kana and Unpai, the film – subtitled “Secret Pulse” – drops audiences into a world battered by giant-monster disasters. Group votes decide how humanity fights back against alien invaders and which romantic storylines play out. Its producers are again drawn from both Japan and Taiwan.

Next Interactive is headed by founder Ronan Wong, who the company says has advised on, produced or distributed every interactive film to receive a commercial theatrical release, across both Western and Eastern markets. Wong served as interactive adviser on Japanese animated feature “Hypnosis Mic – Division Rap Battle,” which grossed JPY2.7 billion ($17 million) from fewer than 100 screens.
“Interactive cinema transforms passive auditoriums into legendary, shared social arenas that simply cannot be replicated at home,” Wong said.

He described the Taiwan launch as a major milestone for the company’s network. “As we prepare to bring these titles and our platform to global territories in 2027, we are proving that when audiences co-create the story together, cinema becomes an unmissable collective event,” Wong said.

articles.title: LA Skins Fest Concludes 20th Year Celebrating Indigenous Artists
paragraphs: The 20th annual LA Skins Fest concluded on Sunday following the five-day celebration of Native American cinema and special screenings at the TCL Chinese Theatre.

Since its founding, the festival has become a platform for Indigenous filmmakers to showcase their work, connect with entertainment industry professionals and reach new audiences. It also extends its mission outside the annual festival through its partnership with the Native American Media Alliance, supporting year-round professional development initiatives that includes writing labs, animation programs, showrunner training, development workshops and youth media education. This year’s LA Skins Fest featured a line-up of narrative features, documentaries, short films and special screenings that recognize Indigenous artists. This year’s festival opened with films presented by Amazon MGM Studios and also included a Netflix screening of “North of North” with actress Anna Lambe and a Cherokee-language screening of “The Rings of Power” followed by a discussion with the actors and Cherokee Film’s language revitalization team.

The festival also began with a Native Youth Studio Tour at Sony Pictures Studios, providing students from Sherman Indian High School an introduction to career opportunities in media, which further reflects the festival’s dedication to supporting future generations of Native American entertainment professionals.

Presented by Paramount Television Studios, the 15th Annual Native American Media Awards hosted by Q’orianka Kilcher and Kiowa Gordon concluded the festival with a celebration of Indigenous filmmakers, writers, actors and creative professionals. Among this year’s winners were Orlando Skidmore for achievement in filmmaking and Sophia Lindholm for achievement in student filmmaking. The emerging filmmaker award was given to Gina East for the narrative film category and Elissa Simons for the documentary category.

The ceremony also recognized the 6th Annual Native American Writer Accelerator Grantees. Sponsored by Netflix, the program selects 12 Indigenous writers to receive financial assistance and opportunities to advance their careers in media. This year’s grantees are Doane Avery, Rachel Baldwin, Ripley Barnes, Sonny Brava, C.J. Caughman, Bryson Chun, Kelly Lynne D’Angelo, Yelyna DeLeon, Marleah Makpiaq LaBelle, Desiree Leiahloha, Jason Marcus and Vlad Perez.

articles.title: Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China
paragraphs: For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China.

For about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang's affairs posed to national security. Bessent was giving voice to China hawks who had felt sidelined by the Trump administration's willingness to sell artificial intelligence chips to China.

They see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China. The resignation of Huang, who pressed the Trump Administration to allow the exports, seemed to signal that the hawks had found new influence in Washington.
By this weekend, Bessent had softened his public resistance to Huang's reinstatement. That came just in time for Nvidia's board to reappoint Huang as CEO at President Donald Trump's urging.

Whether any real damage was done to national security isn't clear. But it is safe to say that the incoming Democratic majority in Congress won't take Trump at his word when he said on CNBC Monday that the Department of Justice "did a pretty good investigation" that exonerated Huang.

Congress will look deeply into the worries Bessent himself raised about Huang's acknowledged romantic relationship with a woman The New York Times and others have reported was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Nvidia's board said it had received assurances from top U.S. officials and had concluded his return wasn't a national security risk.

A top concern is whether China was able to use the affair to help divert Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence chips toward helping its military. Bessent in a Nov. 13 interview with CNBC outlined the stakes.
